subject: Streaming parser failures + latency spike impacting Nimble Commerce (urgent)
messages:
From: Asha Reddy <asha@nimblecommerce.com>
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
Cc: ops+nimble@nimblecommerce.com
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration alerts — streaming errors and latency

Hi Rohan,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx responses from Redwood SDK-based integrations around 08:45 PST this morning. Customers using our live personalization stream are seeing repeated failures: the SDK client throws a parsing error for chunked payloads ("Malformed header: unexpected token") and the stream subsequently stalls. Latency spikes to 2.5–3s per token for affected requests.

Attached is a trimmed log (nimble_error_log_0801.txt) and a sample trace (sdk_trace_0802.json). We rolled back to SDK v2.3.1 and the issue persists; our attempts to disable streaming mode fall back to synchronous calls which increases CPU and reduces throughput. This is impacting checkout personalization for ~12% of sessions.

Can you confirm this is on Redwood's side? We need an ETA for mitigation — our QBR is Thursday and the CSAT impact is already visible.

Thanks,
Asha
Asha Reddy
Head of Integrations, Nimble Commerce
asha@nimblecommerce.com

Attachments:
- nimble_error_log_0801.txt (log snippet)
- sdk_trace_0802.json (trace JSON)

From: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
To: Asha Reddy <asha@nimblecommerce.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Integration alerts — streaming errors and latency

Hi Asha,

Thanks for the quick report and the logs — sorry you're seeing this. I'm escalating now to our runtime team and Marissa (VP R&D) so we can triage with priority. Initial ask: can you confirm the SDK bundle id and whether you're using the CDN-delivered package or an internal bundle? Also, do you still have a recenly-captured pcap or full request/response pair we can use for reproduction?

We'll standby and follow up with an incident update within 60 minutes.

— Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
rohan_mehta@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai (for exec attention)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Integration alerts — streaming errors and latency

Team —

Forwarding Nimble's report. This looks like the same class of parsing/headers regression we saw in the 2.4.x runtime kernel change log last quarter, but we didn't see customer impact then. Marcus, Laura — please take the lead on triage, prioritize repro on a staging pool that mirrors Nimble's config (long-lived prefix caching + chunked streaming). If quick fix isn't possible, prepare rollback plan to previous kernel build.

I'll loop in Customer Success for communication once we have an ETA. Rohan, keep me posted on Nimble's cadence for the QBR.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP R&D, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Integration alerts — streaming errors and latency

Laura and Monica —

I've reproduced the failure locally against a test harness that mimics Nimble's frame sizes and KV cache behavior. The parser throws when it sees a header continuation line starting with lowercase "t" after chunk boundary; that's not tolerated by our relaxed decoder in 2.4.7.

Hypothesis: a change to header normalization in the runtime combined with some CDN edge re-writes is producing an unexpected token sequence. Work plan:
- Create a targeted patch to the streaming parser (restore legacy tolerance for header continuation).
- Add a quick integration test that replays Nimble's sample trace.
- Deploy hotfix to a canary pool and validate throughput/latency.

Estimate: 6–10 hours to a canary with monitoring. If Nimble needs faster mitigation, we can apply a routing rule to send their traffic to the older 2.3 runtime pool within 90 minutes.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, Asha Reddy <asha@nimblecommerce.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Integration alerts — streaming errors and latency

Asha —

We validated a repro against your trace this morning. The quick mitigation we can offer right away is routing Nimble's production traffic to the 2.3.x runtime pool (no code change on your side) which will remove the parsing error and bring latency back to prior baselines. We can perform the routing switch in a staged manner to avoid capacity cliffs.

If you prefer, we can also deploy a parser patch to 2.4.x and run a canary, but that'll take longer. Which do you prefer for the QBR window?

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Infrastructure Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Attachment: nimble_sla_mpa.pdf (contract excerpt)

From: Asha Reddy <asha@nimblecommerce.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
Cc: ops+nimble@nimblecommerce.com
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Integration alerts — streaming errors and latency

Thanks Laura — routing to 2.3.x pool would be ideal for the short term. Please confirm once the staged switch is complete and if we need to modify any retry/backoff on our SDK. We'll schedule a follow-up tech sync to review the root cause and roadmap for the parser fix.

Appreciate the fast response.

— Asha
Asha Reddy
Head of Integrations, Nimble Commerce
asha@nimblecommerce.com
